preamble: Allophonic aspiration of voiceless /k/ to [kʰ] in the onset of a stressed syllable. In English and Standard German the two variants are in complementary distribution: aspirated word-initially and stressed-syllable-initially, unaspirated after /s/ (English) or before a sibilant (German). Turkish likewise usually aspirates syllable-initial /p, t, c, k/.

examples.note: English voiceless stops are aspirated for most native speakers when word-initial or beginning a stressed syllable, but not after /s/ (cf. pin vs. spin).

examples.from: /k/ at the start of a word or stressed syllable, e.g. kalt 'cold'
examples.note: Fortis /p, t, k/ are strongly aspirated at the start of a word or stressed syllable (except before a sibilant), weakly aspirated elsewhere; many southern dialects do not aspirate.
Syllable-initial /p, t, c, k/ are usually aspirated in Turkish.

Pre-Hlai and Proto-Hlai forms are Norquest's (2015) reconstructions as listed in the Wiktionary appendix; Initial Aspiration; Proto-Hlai *kʰ is kept as kʰ in all Hlai languages in the Wikipedia correspondence table.

context: Syllable-initial before stressed vowel = aspirated [kʰ]; post-/s/ = unaspirated [k]
allophones_note: English and German /k/ → [kʰ] in stressed onsets, [k] after /s/ or before a sibilant; Turkish syllable-initial /k/ usually [kʰ]
